ASSIGN: Takes an ordered list of assignments, each is `{"target": "entity.<attr>" | "entity.agent.<attr>" | "<variable>", "expr": "<expression>"}`.
Assignments run in order, so a later one sees what an earlier one wrote.
Targets and expressions both go through core/expressions.py -- a model file never executes Python.
BATCH: Groups entities by count: puts each arrival in the block's store and, as soon as `batch_size` items are waiting, takes exactly that many atomically to form one batch entity.
Members leave live_entities and carry `in_batch` until a SEPARATE splits the batch again.
With `max_wait` set, a PARTIAL batch leaves too: the timer is armed by the arrival that starts a new group and releases whatever is waiting once the oldest member has waited that long.
CREATE: Every model needs at least one CREATE block.
DECIDE: "Chance" mode draws on the block's own RNG against cumulative `probs`; "Condition" mode evaluates each of `conditions` in order and takes the first true one.
"Policy" mode hands the choice to `ctx.controllers[policy]`: the number of actions is simply the number of outgoing links.
DELAY: Use PROCESS instead when the delay is a resource-backed service.
DISPOSE: Waits an optional deletion delay, stamps deletion_time and throughput_time, accrues the entity type's WIP holding cost, and removes the entity from live_entities.
Every model needs at least one DISPOSE block, and every flow that does not lead back to a CREATE must end in one (schema.validate_graph_structured).
HOLD: Infinite mode never releases: the entity stays held in the store for the rest of the run.
That is the documented semantics, not a leak.
LOGIC: Routes an entity through a user-supplied, plain (non-BaseProcess) class defined in nagasim.core.custom_logic.
The class only needs an `execute(self, entity, ctx) -> int` method returning the outgoing link index; `execute(self, entity)` (no ctx) is also accepted.
MATCH: Match `number_to_match` *distinct* entity types; with `match_on` set, only entities whose value of that attribute is equal (Arena's attribute match).
The arriving entity is always stored first, so it can never be dropped ; the match is then taken atomically from the stores, oldest waiting type first, FIFO within a type (and within a value).
MOTION: Seizing, setups, failures, preemption, workers and blocking are PROCESS's.
PROCESS: The most-used block for a simple resource-backed service step.
RECORD: A zero-time block that updates a user-defined statistic and forwards the entity unchanged.
RELEASE: Release everything the entity holds under `resource_name` (a plain resource or a set member), after an optional delay.
Pairs with SEIZE for a hold split across two blocks; raises if the entity never seized that name (fail-loud by design).
SEIZE: Request `quantity` units of `resource_name` (a plain resource or a resource set), honouring priority and the resource's queue discipline, then hold the block's own delay before forwarding.
Pairs with RELEASE for a hold split across two blocks; PROCESS fuses the common Seize-Delay- Release case into one block.
`balk_if` and `renege_after` let an entity leave without ever being served, by the block's second outgoing link.
SIGNAL: After an optional delay, succeeds the named signal event (releasing every HOLD block currently waiting on it) and immediately replaces it with a fresh one -- broadcast, edge-triggered, auto-reset.
STATION: Named entry point of a routing.
